unresolved_added: The Erdos coauthor graph is made undirected and unweighted because joint-publication count and first-cooperation date are unavailable; the lost tie-strength and temporal information is not bounded empirically.
Authors with Erdos number greater than one are omitted to avoid excessive work, without an inclusion sensitivity or retained exclusion list.
The matched random-network construction, seed, degree preservation, and comparator uncertainty are not specified.
Small-world and scale-free descriptions are inferred from one network and limited displayed diagnostics without fit tests or alternative distributions.
The adjusted-cohesion distance transform and weighted/unweighted cases require careful direction and infinity handling; the source does not supply test cases or code.
The sampled Shapley estimator has no seed, convergence statistic, error interval, or guarantee that k=400 is sufficient beyond this displayed case.
A negative Shapley score is interpreted as positive cohesion contribution because lower cohesion is better, but the sign interpretation is not externally validated as influence.
Top-list overlap between Shapley and betweenness is a descriptive comparison, not validation against an independent influence outcome.
The movie-star graph has only a small chosen population and incompletely documented rating-derived edge weights.
Social, career, business, and diplomatic application claims extend descriptive rankings without intervention, fairness, or outcome evidence.
The base PageRank specification leaves citation orientation, dangling-node redistribution, initialization, convergence norm, and iteration trace incomplete.
Citation links differ from web links in time, direction, sparsity, and noise; the transfer analogy is not validated as an equivalent mechanism.
The virtual outside node's residual allocation can dominate a sparse graph, yet its mass conservation and sensitivity are not demonstrated.
Google Scholar Times Cited values lack a query date, corpus policy, duplicate handling, and cross-field normalization.
Rank shifts in Table 5 have no external ground truth, held-out citation outcome, or decision loss, so they cannot establish optimized accuracy.
Institutional and country transfer claims require new populations, relation semantics, time windows, and validation rather than direct reuse of paper ranks.
Systemic-risk language must not be converted into causal or adversarial target-selection advice; use requires authorization, proportionality, monitoring, and harm controls.
The recommendation k>400 is specific to one sample and ranking display; runtime, sampling variation, and error tolerance remain unreported.
The damping conclusion checks only the selected top five rank order over d=0.05..1 and conflates rank invariance with PageRank-value invariance.
